variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is a parameter-efficient way to specialize a pretrained model. The base model stays frozen. Training learns two much smaller matrices inside selected linear layers, and their product becomes a task-specific weight update.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Frozen base
pairs.detail: The pretrained matrix W0 still participates in every forward pass, but its parameters do not receive optimizer updates.
pairs.explanation: The pretrained matrix W0 still participates in every forward pass, but its parameters do not receive optimizer updates.

pairs.label: Low-rank path
pairs.detail: Two matrices, A and B, learn a constrained update delta W = B A through a bottleneck of rank r.
pairs.explanation: Two matrices, A and B, learn a constrained update delta W = B A through a bottleneck of rank r.

pairs.label: Target modules
pairs.detail: The recipe chooses which projections receive adapters: selected attention projections, every attention projection, or a broader set of linear layers.
pairs.explanation: The recipe chooses which projections receive adapters: selected attention projections, every attention projection, or a broader set of linear layers.

pairs.label: Scaling
pairs.detail: Original LoRA applies the update as (alpha / r) B A x.
pairs.explanation: Original LoRA applies the update as (alpha / r) B A x. Rank and alpha are separate choices even when recipes keep their ratio constant.
